title_en: Liu Qingxian v. Xu Biao and Yin Xinyi — dispute over child support
ruling_gist_en: In determining the third-party revocation right in child support cases, it is necessary to clarify whether a parent's payment of child support based on the obligation to support children infringes upon the marital community property rights of the parent after remarriage. Although spouses have equal right to dispose of community property, each spouse also has the right to reasonably dispose of personal income. Unless the child support paid by one party clearly exceeds their financial capacity or there is behavior of transferring community property, it cannot be determined as infringement of community property rights simply because there was no agreement with the current spouse.

full_text_en:
Liu Qingxian v. Xu Biao and Yin Xinyi — dispute over child support

Ruling Summary

The determination of a third party's right to revoke in child support cases requires clarification as to whether a parent's payment of child support based on the duty to support a child infringes upon the marital community property rights after the parent remarries. Although spouses have equal rights to manage community property, each spouse also has the right to reasonably dispose of personal income. Unless the amount of child support paid by one spouse clearly exceeds their financial capacity or constitutes a transfer of marital community property, failure to reach an agreement with the current spouse alone cannot be deemed an infringement of marital community property rights.

Plaintiff: Liu Qingxian, female, 46 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Haidian District, Beijing.

Defendants: Xu Biao, male, 44 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Xuhui District, Shanghai.

Defendant: Yin Xinyi, female, 7 years old, Tujia ethnicity, residing in Minhang District, Shanghai.

Legal Representative: Yin Lifang (mother of Yin Xinyi), 32 years old, Tujia ethnicity, residing in Minhang District, Shanghai.

Plaintiff Liu Qingxian filed a lawsuit with the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai against defendants Xu Biao and Yin Xinyi regarding a child support dispute.

Plaintiff Liu Qingxian alleged: The plaintiff and defendant Xu Biao are spouses, having registered their marriage in April 2008. Defendant Yin Xinyi is Xu Biao's illegitimate daughter. In September 2014, the plaintiff and Xu Biao's father both received a text message from Yin Lifang, Yin Xinyi's mother, informing them that the court had rendered a judgment on July 24, 2014, ordering Xu Biao to pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month for the period from February to June 2014, totaling RMB 100,000, and thereafter to pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month from July 2014 until she reaches the age of 20. Upon questioning by the plaintiff, Xu Biao stated that Yin Lifang had filed a lawsuit in Yin Xinyi's name in April 2014. Upon inquiry with the court, the plaintiff learned that Yin Lifang had also filed a lawsuit in 2008, and the court had rendered a judgment at that time. Now, because Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi violated the relevant provisions of the Marriage Law and seriously infringed upon the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests, the plaintiff requests the revocation of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi and a revised judgment ordering child support of RMB 2,000 per month.

Defendant Yin Xinyi argued: The defendant does not agree with plaintiff Liu Qingxian's claims. A paternity test has confirmed that Yin Xinyi is the child of defendant Xu Biao. Regarding the support of Yin Xinyi, Xu Biao and Yin Xinyi's mother signed several agreements, which later became the subject of litigation due to certain circumstances. The plaintiff also attended the 2008 court hearing. Concerning Yin Xinyi's child support, the court has issued two judgments, both based on litigation arising from the support agreement signed between Xu Biao and Yin Xinyi's mother. Xu Biao's monthly income is RMB 124,000, and his year-end bonus ranges from RMB 500,000 to RMB 1,000,000. Thus, the amount of child support previously awarded by the court for Yin Xinyi does not exceed the legal limits. The quality of a child's support should correspond to the parents' income. The plaintiff's claim of being unaware of Xu Biao's income indicates that the plaintiff and her husband have separate finances, and Xu Biao has the right to dispose of his own property.

Defendant Xu Biao did not provide a defense.

The Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts at first instance:

Plaintiff Liu Qingxian and defendant Xu Biao are spouses, having registered their marriage on April 15, 2008.

According to the effective Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi, Yin Lifang gave birth to defendant Yin Xinyi on September 25, 2007. On April 28, 2008, the Judicial Authentication Center of the Institute of Forensic Science confirmed through paternity testing that defendant Xu Biao is the biological father of Yin Xinyi. The plaintiff and Xu Biao's daughter was born on November 1, 2008.

On May 16, 2008, Yin Lifang and defendant Xu Biao signed a written "Agreement on Child Support and Property Division," stipulating that Yin Xinyi would be raised by Yin Lifang, and Xu Biao would pay child support of RMB 20,000 per month until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. In August 2008, Yin Xinyi filed a lawsuit [Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi], alleging that Xu Biao had only paid two months of child support after signing the agreement and requesting that Xu Biao pay child support of RMB 20,000 per month from December 2007 until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. The court rendered a judgment on November 20, 2008, ordering Xu Biao to pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 10,000 per month from December 2007 until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. Neither party appealed.

On June 5, 2014, defendant Yin Xinyi filed another lawsuit [Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi], claiming that in April 2010, Xu Biao promised to increase Yin Xinyi's child support to RMB 12,000 per month; in October 2011, Xu Biao further increased the child support to RMB 20,000 per month and fulfilled this obligation until January 2014, but thereafter ceased payment. Yin Xinyi requested that Xu Biao pay child support of RMB 20,000 per month from February 2014 until she reaches the age of 20. The court rendered a judgment on July 24, 2014: (1) Xu Biao shall pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month for the period from February to June 2014, totaling RMB 100,000, within ten days after this judgment becomes effective; (2) Xu Biao shall pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month from July 2014 until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. Neither party appealed after the judgment.

During the trial, plaintiff Liu Qingxian emphasized that she only learned of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi on September 9 of this year. She argued that the child support amount and duration set by that judgment lack legal basis. She claimed Xu Biao's monthly after-tax income is not RMB 124,000, that the plaintiff and her husband have a daughter born after their marriage, that they did not adopt a separate property regime, and that Xu Biao made the promise under duress. Therefore, the judgment infringed upon the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests. The plaintiff also provided proof that she is currently unemployed and requested the revocation and revision of the judgment. Yin Xinyi provided evidence that Xu Biao's current pre-tax monthly income is RMB 124,000, emphasizing that Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi was rendered based on the agreement between Xu Biao and Yin Lifang regarding Yin Xinyi's support, not a dispute over child support. Xu Biao had no objection to the agreement, and since Yin Xinyi was born before Xu Biao's marriage to the plaintiff, the court's judgment did not affect the plaintiff's marital family life.

The Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance:

During the trial of Case No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi, the plaintiff Liu Qingxian was not joined as a third party due to reasons not attributable to her. Secondly, Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi ordered Xu Biao to pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month from February 2014 until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20, while Xu Biao had registered his marriage with the plaintiff on April 15, 2008. Thirdly, as there is no evidence that the plaintiff and Xu Biao adopted a separate property regime after marriage, the child support payable under that judgment effectively constitutes the marital community property of the plaintiff and Xu Biao. Spouses have equal rights to dispose of community property. Finally, there is also no evidence that the plaintiff consented to Xu Biao's promise to Yin Lifang regarding Yin Xinyi's child support. In summary, the judgment clearly involves the plaintiff's economic interests. As the plaintiff claims the judgment infringes upon her civil rights and interests, and her lawsuit was filed within the statutory period, her claim is established, and her revocation action is permissible. As for the appropriate amount and duration of Yin Xinyi's current child support, the relevant parties may resolve the dispute through further negotiation or litigation; this case does not address that issue. Xu Biao's failure to appear in court without just cause is deemed a waiver of his right to defend.

Accordingly, the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai, pursuant to Article 56, Paragraph 3, and Article 144 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 24, 2014:

Revoke Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi of the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai.

Yin Xinyi, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The first-instance court erred in its application of law. The content of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi is not erroneous and does not meet the conditions for revocation. This case concerns the support of a child born before defendant Xu Biao's marriage, which is different from the general disposition of marital community property. Moreover, plaintiff Liu Qingxian stated during the trial that she and Xu Biao manage their respective properties separately without interference. Yin Xinyi has reason to believe that they have a certain degree of separate financial arrangement. As long as Xu Biao has the financial capacity to pay, Liu Qingxian has no right to intervene. Therefore, Yin Xinyi requests the reversal of the original judgment and a revised ruling dismissing Liu Qingxian's original claims.

The appellee Liu Qingxian argued: The first-instance judgment is correct. The agreement between original defendant Xu Biao and Yin Lifang regarding appellant Yin Xinyi's child support infringes upon Liu Qingxian's lawful rights and interests and is therefore void. Paying child support for Yin Xinyi from age 18 to 20 is not a legal obligation of Xu Biao. The agreement for Xu Biao to pay Yin Xinyi child support of RMB 20,000 per month until she reaches adulthood seriously infringes upon Liu Qingxian's lawful rights and interests. Liu Qingxian requests the dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment.

The original defendant Xu Biao indicated agreement with appellee Liu Qingxian's position.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

Whether appellee Liu Qingxian's right to request the revocation of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi can be established depends on the following two points:

First, regarding the content of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi: After an effective judgment in 2008 confirmed that original defendant Xu Biao should pay child support at a rate of RMB 10,000 per month, Xu Biao issued promises on April 12, 2010, and October 13, 2011, increasing the child support to RMB 12,000 per month and RMB 20,000 per month, respectively, until appellant Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. In both promises, he explicitly stated, "If any legal dispute arises in the future due to any reason (such as family pressure or court proceedings), I request the court to render a judgment in accordance with this will." Thereafter, Xu Biao fulfilled this commitment until January 2014. The amount and duration of child support are first determined by agreement between the parents; if no agreement is reached, the court decides. In this case, Xu Biao made clear commitments regarding the amount and duration of child support for Yin Xinyi. After reviewing the statements of both parties, the evidence presented, and Xu Biao's income, the first-instance court confirmed that Xu Biao should perform according to his commitments and accordingly ordered Xu Biao to pay child support of RMB 20,000 per month until Yin Xinyi reaches the age of 20. The court finds that the content of Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi is not improper.

Second, whether original defendant Xu Biao's commitment regarding the amount and duration of child support for appellant Yin Xinyi infringes upon appellee Liu Qingxian's marital community property rights. To resolve this issue, it is first necessary to clarify whether a parent's payment of child support based on the duty to support a child infringes upon the marital community property rights after the parent remarries. Parents have a legal obligation to support minor children. Illegitimate children enjoy equal rights with legitimate children. A biological father or mother who does not directly raise an illegitimate child shall bear the child's living and education expenses until the child can live independently. Although spouses have equal rights to manage community property, each spouse also has the right to reasonably dispose of personal income. Failure to reach an agreement with the current spouse alone cannot be deemed an infringement of marital community property rights, unless the amount of child support paid by one spouse clearly exceeds their financial capacity or constitutes a transfer of marital community property. In this case, although the amount of child support Xu Biao promised to pay is indeed higher than the general standard, when both parents' financial conditions permit, they should do their best to provide better living and learning conditions for their children. The amount of child support Xu Biao promised to pay has always been within his personal income capacity, and Xu Biao's income has been stable or increasing over the years, while the proportion of Yin Xinyi's child support relative to his income has actually decreased. Therefore, there is no act of transferring marital community property. Accordingly, the court finds that Xu Biao's commitment regarding the amount and duration of child support for Yin Xinyi did not infringe upon Liu Qingxian's marital community property rights.

In summary, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 25 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on April 23, 2015:

1. Revoke Civil Judgment No. 3 (2014) Xu Min Yi (Min) Che Zi of the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai;
2. Dismiss Liu Qingxian's claim to revoke Civil Judgment No. 60 (2014) Xu Shao Min Chu Zi of the Xuhui District People's Court of Shanghai.

This judgment is final.
